title: Lurie signs data center moratorium, pausing new development
key_facts: Mayor Daniel Lurie signed on Friday 16 Oct 2026 a moratorium that pauses data-centre development citywide for 45 days (San Francisco Standard).
The ordinance, authored by Supervisor Shamann Walton, tasks the San Francisco Planning Department with studying the impacts of data centres and developing controls for them.
The Board of Supervisors approved it unanimously last week after Board President Rafael Mandelman fast-tracked it.
Friday was the deadline for Lurie to sign; without his signature the moratorium would have taken effect anyway.

Lurie said the city will 'develop a thoughtful, responsible framework' prioritising community needs, low electricity rates and clean water and air; his statement did not explicitly mention data centres.
The Standard reported in September that the Planning Department did not know how many data centres exist in the city; Data Center Map counts at least six, two of them in Bayview-Hunters Point.

why_it_matters_hint: San Francisco will pause new data centres for 45 days while it finds out how many it has and what controls are needed.
